facts.text: A scenario catalog is a traceable inventory whose entries identify the hazardous interaction, requirement or hazard source, applicable domain tags, expected behaviour and parameter-family ID.
facts.quote: Each entry identifies the hazardous interaction, its requirement or hazard source, the applicable domain tags, the expected behaviour and the ID of the parameter family it belongs to.

facts.text: ISO 34504:2024 formalises scenario categorisation using tags.
facts.quote: ISO 34504:2024 formalises scenario categorisation with tags

facts.text: ISO 34505:2025, dated June 2025, specifies that resulting test cases carry identifiers, objectives, inputs, steps, test platform and expected results.
facts.quote: ISO 34505:2025 (June 2025) specifies that the resulting test cases carry identifiers, objectives, inputs, steps, test platform and expected results.

facts.text: ISO 34504:2024 and ISO 34505:2025 are road-vehicle standards whose information structure transfers to off-road scenario catalogs.
facts.quote: Both are road-vehicle standards whose information structure transfers

facts.text: The off-road adequacy of ISO 34504:2024 and ISO 34505:2025 has not been established.
facts.quote: their off-road adequacy has not been established.

facts.text: The scenario catalog follows the three-level abstraction adopted from the PEGASUS project into ISO 34501 to ISO 34505: functional, logical and concrete scenarios.
facts.quote: The catalog follows the three-level abstraction adopted from the PEGASUS project into ISO 34501 to 34505

facts.text: Functional scenarios describe interactions in words; an example is the EMESRT storyboard “vehicle reversing towards a person”.
facts.quote: functional scenarios in words (for example the EMESRT storyboard "vehicle reversing towards a person")

facts.text: Logical scenarios specify parameter ranges; the passage's example includes person distance from 0 to 30 m, approach angle, machine speed from 0 to 15 km/h and dust density.
facts.quote: logical scenarios with parameter ranges (person distance 0 to 30 m, approach angle, machine speed 0 to 15 km/h, dust density)

facts.text: Concrete scenarios specify fixed parameter values.
facts.quote: concrete scenarios with fixed values.

facts.text: The functional–logical–concrete scenario hierarchy is well established in automated-driving research, but the original work and most validation experience are on-road.
facts.quote: The hierarchy is well established in automated-driving research, although the original work and most validation experience are on-road.

facts.text: Directly applicable safety standards anchor the off-road content of the scenario catalog.
facts.quote: For the off-road content, the directly applicable safety standards anchor the catalog.

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022, dated January 2022, applies to earth-moving machinery, mobile underground mining machinery and road-construction machinery.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-1:2022 (January 2022) applies to earth-moving machinery, mobile underground mining machinery and road-construction machinery

facts.text: ISO 21815-1:2022 explicitly includes object detection, warning and automatic intervention through speed reduction or motion inhibition.
facts.quote: explicitly includes object detection, warning and automatic intervention through speed reduction or motion inhibition.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3:2023, dated August 2023, defines the risk area and risk level for forward and reverse motion.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3:2023 (August 2023) defines the risk area and risk level for forward and reverse motion.

facts.text: ISO 16001:2017, dated November 2017 and confirmed in 2023, sets performance and test requirements for object-detection systems and visibility aids.
facts.quote: ISO 16001:2017 (November 2017, confirmed 2023) sets performance and test requirements for object-detection systems and visibility aids

facts.text: ISO 16001:2017 requires a detection time of at most 300 ms for object-detection systems and visibility aids.
facts.quote: including a detection time of at most 300 ms.

facts.text: Draft ISO 21815 Part 4 covers swing and rotation and is “under publication”, with an expected publication date of October 2026.
facts.quote: Part 4 (swing and rotation) is "under publication" with an expected date of October 2026

facts.text: Draft ISO 21815 Part 5 covers other motions such as articulation and reversing trailers and is at the final proof stage, with publication planned for November 2026.
facts.quote: Part 5 (other motions such as articulation and reversing trailers) is at the final proof stage with planned publication in November 2026

facts.text: Draft ISO 21815 Parts 4 and 5 define risk areas for motions performed by off-road machines and should be tracked during the project.
facts.quote: both define risk areas for motions these machines have and should be tracked during the project.

facts.text: ISO 21815 Parts 1, 3, 4 and 5 and ISO 16001 do not set statistical sample sizes or simulation-credibility rules.
facts.quote: None of these standards sets statistical sample sizes or simulation-credibility rules.
